name: Participatory democracy
summary: Participatory democracy holds that citizens should take a direct and continuing part in the decisions that affect their lives, not only vote for representatives. It sees participation as educative, building the capacities of citizens, and extends it from government to workplaces, communities and schools. Most adherents combine direct mechanisms such as assemblies, referendums and participatory budgeting with representative institutions.
scope: The modern participatory-democracy tradition: Rousseau as forerunner, Carole Pateman's Participation and Democratic Theory (1970), C. B. Macpherson's participatory model, and the New Left's Port Huron Statement (1962). It excludes deliberative-democracy theory in its own right and direct-democracy purism; positions outside democratic procedure are mostly low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Carole Pateman
keyFigures.role: Political theorist whose 1970 book Participation and Democratic Theory set out the educative case for participation.

keyFigures.name: C. B. Macpherson
keyFigures.role: Political theorist who proposed a participatory model of democracy in The Life and Times of Liberal Democracy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Participatory democrats back broad social provision but the sources do not address healthcare; inferred from the Port Huron call for democratic control of economic resources.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the concern that economic participation requires dignified, non-stultifying work and rough equality of standing.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Port Huron subjects major economic resources to democratic regulation, implying distrust of unregulated markets, but the topic is not directly argued.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents want democratic control of major resources, yet participatory theorists split between public, cooperative and regulated-private forms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pateman and Macpherson link participation to reducing economic inequality, so higher taxes on the wealthy fit, though taxation is not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Unions and workplace bodies are natural sites of worker participation, which Pateman treats as the most important arena for democratic education.

property-fundamental.rationale: Participatory writers subject economic resources to democratic participation, so property is not an absolute right; inferred, not stated.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from Port Huron's call to open major economic resources to democratic regulation and participation; the sources do not discuss regulating corporations as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts clash with the aim of equalising the capacity to participate; inferred from Pateman's equality argument.

worker-ownership.rationale: Pateman stresses democratising authority structures in industry; worker self-management is the standard form, though ownership as such is a step beyond the sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the emphasis on free, independent citizens who take part without fear of officials.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The tradition says nothing on drug policy, and adherents hold varied views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; participatory democrats value open public debate but also inclusive participation, so adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Participatory democracy opposes leaving decisions to elites and favours citizens deciding directly, so a leader bypassing gridlock is contrary to it.

state-harmful.rationale: It seeks to democratise the state and combine participation with representation, not to abolish it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no distinct position follows from participatory principles.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from Port Huron's critique of military investment in the Cold War status quo and its preference for civic power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No position in the tradition; adherents are divided.

decide-locally.rationale: Participation is most feasible in communities and workplaces, and Port Huron wants people to share in decisions that shape their lives, which favours local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Port Huron's humanistic view of people's capacity for reason and creativity.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's emphasis on independence and community participation does not endorse fixed family structures.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from equal standing and inclusion as participatory values.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from personal independence and decisions over one's own life.

more-religion-public.rationale: The tradition is secular in its justification of authority; no explicit stance, inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Port Huron says the promise of equality rang hollow before the facts of Black life and treats the civil-rights struggle as a formative cause.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The participatory-democracy sources never discuss the nature of gender, and adherents hold varied views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The tradition is about the form of decision-making, not national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Port Huron seeks a social movement for deep change rather than deference to established institutions; participatory reformers also use incremental experiments, so only mildly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inclusion of all affected people in decisions suggests opposition, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Participatory democrats worry about distant decision-makers but may favour global cooperation; not addressed.

free-trade.rationale: The sources say nothing about trade policy, and participatory democrats range from free-traders to critics of globalisation.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; Port Huron criticises Cold War nationalism, inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Port Huron criticises Cold War militarism, but participation theory says nothing on intervention for human rights, so adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: The tradition concerns how decisions are made among those affected and does not address whether borders should be open.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition does not take a position on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Citizens' assemblies on climate (France 2019) are cited examples, but the sources do not give the ideology a view on policy drasticness.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Port Huron is sceptical of technocratic, impersonal solutions; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Port Huron fears nuclear weapons; nuclear power is not discussed, so weak inference.

revolution-justified.rationale: The tradition mostly seeks change through movements and participation; violence is not endorsed in the sources.

experts-over-public.rationale: Participatory democracy holds that ordinary people should decide matters affecting them; Pateman contrasts it with elitist theories that rely on a few leaders.

central-planning.rationale: Port Huron seeks democratic participation in economic decisions, not top-down planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership under democratic control fits the economic democracy strand, though markets are not discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: No participatory-democracy source takes a position on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the equality concern that unequal wealth undermines equal participation.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is not discussed in the sources, and adherents are divided over unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariff policy is outside the sources; adherents could favour protection for communities or oppose it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Participatory writers prefer democratic decision-making over state direction; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from cooperativists to socialists.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not part of the participatory program, which reforms ownership and authority within existing economies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The sources want democratic control over economic decisions, not abolition of central banks and a market-run currency.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are not discussed; participation in industry is favoured but not in corporatist form.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia defines participatory democracy as citizens taking part directly in decisions, which leaves no room for a single ruling party; no source discusses one-party rule as such.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from the principle that citizens share in the decisions that affect them; the sources do not discuss monarchy, and a purely ceremonial crown does not take decisions away from citizens.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents are committed democrats who want more democracy, but the sources do not take up the 'even when voters choose badly' clause, and Pateman blames apathy on elitism rather than voters.

direct-votes.rationale: Wikipedia presents binding referendums and popular initiatives as tools of participatory democracy, though many adherents prefer deliberation or hybrid models and some (Landemore) worry about referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Workplace democracy is central, but participatory democrats usually combine councils with representative institutions rather than replacing parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; local self-rule is favoured but secession is not a stated position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Pateman opposes elitist theory that treats a few as leaders and the rest as apathetic; participation is meant to develop everyone's capacity.

political-violence-never.rationale: The sources describe non-violent civic participation but do not state a doctrine on violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Port Huron condemns the Cold War and the Bomb; character is built through participation, not war. Inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular, reason-based grounds for collective decisions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Laws made by participating citizens, not by scripture; inferred from the participatory principle.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed; collective control of public functions is implied.

military-superiority.rationale: Port Huron criticises military investment in the Cold War status quo.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive participation of all affected people suggests rejection.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Macpherson draws on Marxist-influenced analysis, but the participatory tradition does not adopt class conflict as the engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Pateman and Macpherson want greater equality, particularly equal capacity to participate, but not strictly equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the principle that communities decide matters affecting them; not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not discussed in the sources, so no stated position can be drawn.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from preference for decisions near those affected.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Port Huron values community, and politics brings people out of isolation; inferred rejection of self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Port Huron centres individual independence alongside participation; not discussed directly.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources are about decision-making and do not take a view on the intrinsic value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is outside the scope of participatory democratic theory.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Port Huron criticises stultifying work and alienation but does not reject industrial society; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition favours democratic control over change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Enhancement technology is not addressed by participatory theory, and adherents are split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Delegating decisions to algorithms conflicts with citizens deciding for themselves, though online tools are used; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from independence and free political activity.

restore-past-order.rationale: Port Huron seeks social change toward more participation; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The sources do not discuss pragmatism versus ideology; participatory democracy itself is a principled commitment about process.

direct-action.rationale: Split: Port Huron calls for a social movement and Occupy assemblies are cited as examples, while much of the tradition works through institutions such as participatory budgeting.

means-match-ends.rationale: Participatory democracy treats participation as both the means and the goal, as in Port Huron's 'democracy of individual participation'.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No source suggests abandoning agriculture or industry; Port Huron seeks reform of work, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Port Huron wants work to be educative, not stultifying, but not abolition of specialisation; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is not discussed; Pateman and Macpherson stress equality but not a need-based rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Work and economy that serve human needs fit Port Huron's economic values; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not part of the participatory-democratic doctrine; Macpherson is critical of market society but adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial power by one class contradicts the broad participation of all citizens.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organisation is not addressed in the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; Port Huron criticises Cold War economic and military investments but does not claim inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: collective decisions about public budgets (participatory budgeting) presuppose legitimate taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: The harm principle is not discussed by the participatory authors opened, and the ideology is silent on limits to state action.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Participatory theory neither affirms nor denies group rights in the sources opened.

conscription.rationale: Port Huron's emphasis on independence and its Cold War critique make this unlikely; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participation (voice) in decisions is the core of the ideology.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are participants in self-government, not customers; inferred from the core conception of citizenship.

positive-liberty.rationale: Pateman and Macpherson hold that people need the material and educational means to participate and develop their capacities.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not claim that universities and media outrank elected officials; Port Huron focuses on universities as sites of participation.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; inconsistent with the equality premise of equal participation.

organic-representation.rationale: Participation is by individuals, including in workplaces and communities, but not as a replacement of parties through organic bodies; inferred.

total-state.rationale: State direction of all life contradicts people sharing in decisions that shape their lives.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical national renewal is not part of participatory theory, which is about citizen decision-making; inferred mild disagreement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; Port Huron critiques militarism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personal fealty is the opposite of citizens' direct participation; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; contradicts the autonomy of the participating citizen.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of knowledge and power is not addressed in the sources.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not take a position on universal moral truths, and Port Huron's appeal to reason is not developed into a metaethics.

single-common-good.rationale: Participatory theorists generally stress deliberation among differing interests and views; Barber-type unity is not in the sources.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israel and Zionism are not addressed in participatory-democracy sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in the sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a topic of participatory-democracy sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pateman sees industry as the most important site of democratic education and stresses democratising its authority structures; Port Huron opens production to democratic participation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want participation in schools but have no stated voucher view.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy on deficits is not covered by the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; Macpherson criticises liberal democracy's dependence on the market.

rule-by-example.rationale: Authority should rest on participation rather than rulers' moral example; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; self-rule is valued but nation-state framing is not.

force-without-un.rationale: Port Huron criticises Cold War militarism; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Port Huron cites reason and reflectiveness but does not declare faith excluded.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology's aim of including everyone affected in decisions suggests mild opposition to restricting welfare by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; compulsion conflicts with Port Huron's view of work as chosen and educative.

class-collaboration.rationale: Workplace democracy reduces employer-worker hierarchy, but the sources do not frame it as either collaboration or class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; nothing in participatory theory calls for sacrificing cultural institutions, and Port Huron treats universities as valuable sites of participation.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc against Western powers is not addressed in the sources.

workers-nation.rationale: The sources do not discuss whether workers should organise nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal participation by all citizens is the premise; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans are not part of participatory-democratic thought.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Port Huron condemns racial bigotry and holds that the claim of equality rang hollow before the facts of Black life.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Macpherson's critique of liberal democracy touches this, but the tradition does not state it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; weak inference from environmental-assembly examples.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilation is not discussed; inclusion of all affected people suggests mild opposition to demanding cultural abandonment.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Participatory democrats emphasise participation more than electoral formulas; SEP covers PR but no adherent position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; Port Huron criticises the Cold War status quo.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender hierarchy is not analysed in the sources opened, so no stated position.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Wikipedia reports participatory budgeting is credited with reducing clientelism and corruption; adherents view distant elites as insulated from ordinary people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; contradicts equal worth and independence.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; accountability fits democratic control.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Participatory democracy wants broad collective decision-making on economic and social life.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to equality and independence in Port Huron; not addressed directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal participation presupposes it; Port Huron quotes 'all men are created equal' and holds it should be real.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist debate is outside participatory democracy's concerns.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not discussed in participatory-democracy sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law pluralism is not addressed by the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from independence of individuals.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter law is outside the sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in schools is not addressed; Port Huron discusses universities but not this question.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; contradicts the participatory emphasis on broadening decision-making.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Citizens deciding directly or through representatives accountable to them is the basis of Rousseau-derived participatory theory.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not addressed by participatory theory.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts the equal inclusion of all affected people in decisions, though the sources do not discuss it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The sources do not address a non-aggression principle; adherents support collective decisions that bind everyone.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Port Huron emphasises community and cooperation; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banning parties is not discussed; adherents balance inclusion against protecting democratic order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Participation to resist arbitrary power fits, though the republican framing is not used in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; hybrid models keep representative institutions but do not discuss separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The theory is that ordinary people develop political capacity through participation, which contradicts a vanguard leading them.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Wikipedia notes participation is seen as giving weaker actors more say; policy priority is inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales are outside the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from support for worker participation and direct action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; institutional explanations suit the tradition.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not discussed; participatory democrats value inclusion of diverse people and Port Huron condemns racial bigotry, so mild disagreement is inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Wikipedia notes Athens' random selection as an early example, and SEP discusses sortition; participatory democrats tend to accept it as one tool, though not as a replacement for all elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on citizens' independence.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed in the sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of media by the ruling party contradicts free participation and public deliberation.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is not discussed; it concentrates power away from citizens, which the ideology opposes.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are not addressed; the ideology's inclusive aims suggest mild disagreement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a documented demand of participatory theory.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Participatory models stress citizens' own deliberation over party command; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions are not addressed; participatory democrats worry about distant decision-making but also back cooperation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A head of state commanding the forces and picking ministers concentrates power in one person, against the participatory principle.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchy is contrary to participation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars contradicts citizen self-government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist doctrine outside participatory theory.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship for moral character is not discussed; free public debate underlies participatory deliberation, so mild disagreement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; concentrated power is disfavoured.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's stress on keeping representatives accountable to citizens; the sources do not name recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not discussed beyond Port Huron's Cold War critique; no clear position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed in the sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed citizenry is not discussed in the sources.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural versus urban life is not discussed in the sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Participatory theory seeks educated, capable ordinary citizens and does not argue that graduates are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not addressed in the sources.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Port Huron's humanistic values.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not discussed; inferred mild agreement from the ideology's educative, inclusive orientation.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Port Huron's reason and reflectiveness.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is outside the sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed; inclusion of residents in decisions suggests mild disagreement.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive participation implies support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are not addressed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Port Huron values independence and individuality; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt is not addressed in the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economics is not addressed, though Port Huron links democracy to economic participation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the sources praise citizens' assemblies such as Ireland's as participatory tools, but none discusses rewriting a constitution through an elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Contradicts participation as an end and as the educator of citizens.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed in the sources opened.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Port Huron says the presence of the Bomb created fear and criticises Cold War military investment, suggesting opposition to national arsenals.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; more direct citizen choice fits the ideology.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; insulating economic decisions from democratic control runs against the principle.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions are not addressed in the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Port Huron subjects economic resources to democratic regulation, implying property is conditional.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterisation of the USSR is not part of the participatory tradition's sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is not addressed, though deliberative mechanisms like climate assemblies are cited.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; consent of the people affected is central, so inferred agreement.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state subordination is not discussed in the sources.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ceremonial role of a head of state is outside the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; coercing communities conflicts with people deciding for themselves.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; local autonomy fits the preference for decisions close to those affected.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred ruler contradicts citizens' direct role in decisions.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern with economic inequality.

character-from-environment.rationale: Pateman holds that participation shapes citizens' capacities and character, which implies formation by circumstances and institutions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler above the law contradicts the principle that citizens take part in making the decisions that bind them.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not discussed in the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; participatory theory favours a hybrid of direct and representative elements, but not classical few-and-many mixing.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to ordinary citizens' own agency.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine outside participatory theory.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not addressed in the sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not addressed in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on co-nationals abroad are not discussed; the ideology's focus on those affected by decisions suggests mild disagreement.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy contradicts the independence of individuals that Port Huron treats as a core value.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are not discussed in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; self-governing communities fit the principle of self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Zionism-diaspora debate is outside participatory theory.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not a doctrine of participatory theory, though Macpherson draws on it.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; democratic regulation of concentrated economic power fits Port Huron.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Participatory democrats value popular decisions but the sources do not address courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; inclusion in decision-making bodies fits equality of participation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are not part of participatory-democracy sources.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern for working conditions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Port Huron wants work with incentives beyond money, but the sources do not call for replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A small armed group acting for the people contradicts broad participation.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Port Huron seeks to replace power based on privilege and possession with participation by all.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History teaching is not addressed in the sources.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by some over others for their improvement contradicts self-government and Pateman's rejection of elitism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; education is meant to build independent participants.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Port Huron's attention to racial injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism's adaptability is not addressed; Macpherson's critique is of liberal democracy rather than a crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed; the ideology emphasises self-government.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency strategy is not addressed in the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis outside participatory theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts Port Huron's condemnation of racial bigotry.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed in the sources opened.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not addressed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elected rulers fit the consent principle, though participatory democrats want more than election.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; participation models rely on collective decisions, and consensus procedures vary.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with citizens' sovereignty.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is not discussed; participatory theory is about direct involvement beyond parliaments.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the participatory-democratic sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Participatory democracy seeks equal standing rather than charity from the privileged; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Politics is treated as a positive activity that brings people out of isolation, per Port Huron; participation is the core value.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Port Huron's critique of apathy and 'politics without publics' suggests the view, though not explicitly in the opened text.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of the participatory sources, though the apathy-from-elitism argument is related.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems and dependency theory are not part of the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for natives is not discussed; broad inclusion of those affected favours disagreement.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist-party autonomy is outside participatory theory.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not addressed; Port Huron criticises power politics, inferred mild disagreement.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; equal participation of all citizens.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional founding values are not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Port Huron criticises both Cold War camps but the sources do not state the equivalence claim.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The historical claim is not addressed; Port Huron's attention to racial injustice suggests mild disagreement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is not discussed; participatory democrats would favour local deliberation but have no stated side.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not discussed; participatory democracy is presented as broadly applicable, but the sources do not address cultural differences.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are not addressed in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; rule by credentialed officials contrasts with the participatory emphasis.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from personal independence.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Representatives accountable to citizens fit the hybrid, participation-first approach; Plotke's hybrid view keeps representation as a complement, so not strongly.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure is not addressed in the sources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; participatory budgeting extends democratic control over budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: Not discussed; inclusion of all participants suggests language support, but no stated position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests for discrimination are not addressed in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Port Huron criticises work and life driven by money incentives and wants other values; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Port Huron's critique of Cold War militarism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Port Huron's critique of Cold War militarism and Soviet/US power politics.

corporate-influence.rationale: Port Huron says economic resources should be subject to democratic regulation, and participatory democrats see money as limiting equal participation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would worry about civil-society restrictions, but there is no stated position.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; local control of housing markets is outside the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aim of work that is meaningful and incomes enabling participation.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic-peace thesis is not part of participatory-democracy sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; Rousseau-derived participation grounds the duty to obey in participation.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed in the sources beyond Port Huron's critique of Cold War interventions.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims about minorities contradict equal inclusion of citizens and have no support in the sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Informed participation requires access to information; Wikipedia presents deliberative forums and consultation as ways to inform citizens before deciding.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed; participatory groups range from formal assemblies to informal movements.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion is not discussed; the ideology's inclusive logic suggests mild disagreement.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual submission to a leading power contradicts the self-government the ideology prizes.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Port Huron criticises anti-communism and Cold War logic, though it also opposes Soviet-style tyranny.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are not addressed in the sources.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not discussed; Macpherson and Port Huron critique capitalism's effects, but the sources do not rate its historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not addressed; self-governing communities fit participatory aims, but the specific property regime is not stated.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; deliberately shifting populations conflicts with equal inclusion, so mild disagreement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Port Huron's New Left rejected both Cold War poles in favour of participation; inferred for the core strand.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; denial of established history conflicts with informed deliberation.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; contradicts equal rights and independence.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppression of opposition is incompatible with citizens taking part in decisions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rule of colonies for the benefit of the ruling country contradicts self-government, the core of the ideology.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law doctrine that participatory-democracy sources do not address.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would reject religious criteria for legitimacy but the sources are silent.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The defining claim of the ideology: citizens should take part directly in decisions that affect their lives, as Port Huron's 'democracy of individual participation' and Pateman's educative participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed in the opened sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild agreement from the ideology's inclusive aims.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is associated with the New Left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from Port Huron's demand that work be educative and self-directed rather than stultifying; the sources do not frame this as alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Claims of cultural incompatibility contradict the equal inclusion of all citizens in participation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority rests on the participation of citizens, derived from Rousseau-style popular sovereignty.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild agreement from the aim of equal voice for workers.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not discussed; adherents want more democratic control than a social market offers, but the sources do not rule on it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Port Huron's anti-Bomb stance does not amount to abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; inconsistent with equal participation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Port Huron criticises both Cold War camps; weak inference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is incompatible with citizen participation.

property-franchise.rationale: Restricting the vote contradicts broad, equal participation.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not addressed in the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist-Lukacsian theory is not addressed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Macpherson's and Pateman's concern that economic inequality undermines political equality.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not discussed; rule by known laws fits a citizen-governed polity, so mild agreement is inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Wikipedia and Pateman's account rest on broad participation, and Port Huron condemns racial bigotry.

online-participation.rationale: Wikipedia lists online forums and consultations among participatory mechanisms and notes liquid democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Informed participation requires publicly traceable decision-making; inferred from deliberative-process descriptions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotting a religious minority contradicts equal inclusion and has no support in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Citizens' assemblies such as Ireland's 2011 assembly and France's 2019 climate convention are cited as participatory instruments.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The tradition is about democratic procedure and takes no position on religious doctrine; adherents are split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Port Huron Statement calls for democratic control of economic resources and criticizes concentrated corporate power over citizens' lives.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's commitment to equal participation and rights; the sources do not discuss military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: participatory democrats value citizen choice, which cuts against state-imposed worldviews in schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss policing; the tradition's concern is democratic participation.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: it favors inclusion of all groups in decisions but sources do not address consociational executive arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron Statement's call for public democratic control of resources rather than reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; term limits widen participation but the tradition is mainly concerned with citizen participation in decisions.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: delegation widens citizen control over policy, but it is not discussed and some adherents prefer direct participation over delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no documented position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to equal participation for all citizens; religious offices are not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its call to extend participation and equality to all spheres of life, including the household; not discussed directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Its principle that people should take part in decisions affecting their lives extends naturally to local residents; not stated explicitly.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron call for democratic control of economic resources; rent policy is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources do not address intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its stress on free, voluntary civic participation as educative.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The Port Huron Statement criticises the Cold War arms race; basing of weapons is inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is about internal democratic procedure.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Port Huron Statement wants work to be educative and economic resources democratically controlled, which is inferred as favouring reward for work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's pacifist and civil-rights nonviolence in the Port Huron Statement; not stated as an absolute ban.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; it is a procedural tradition with no stake in national origins, inferred as sceptical.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its civic, egalitarian and secular emphasis.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is seen as citizens' participation, institutions and interests, not cosmic struggle; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Its commitment to equality and wide participation, including racial equality in the Port Huron Statement, implies economic roles open to all.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron call for democratic control of work and unions answering to members, though unions are not discussed explicitly.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Participatory democrats seek democratic control of economic resources and workers' say, but the sources do not define socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the call for democratic public control of economic resources; local services are not discussed directly.

second-chamber.rationale: Participatory theory addresses citizen involvement rather than the number of chambers; sortition-based chambers are one proposal.

municipal-property.rationale: Port Huron favours democratic control of economic resources but not specifically municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Adherents favour local assemblies, but whether joint bodies may bind members is not addressed.

family-wage.rationale: Wage design is not addressed by participatory theory.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation is not addressed by the tradition.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not addressed by the tradition.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Financial privacy is not addressed; adherents split between privacy and public accountability.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not addressed; open participation arguments could cut either way.

person-over-state.rationale: The Port Huron Statement sets out a democracy of individual participation in which people are ends, not instruments.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The tradition is about procedure; the Port Huron text speaks of human worth but takes no stance on spiritual needs in politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from its preference for decisions at the level closest to citizens, which favours entrenched local power, though sources do not address this.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not addressed by the tradition.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density is not addressed by the tradition.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Port Huron Statement calls for racial equality and common participation, which implies politics not organised along racial lines.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents' stance on identity pride varies.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron critique of Cold War militarism; no explicit statement on defensive war.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Participatory democracy is a theory of citizen decision-making, not nationhood; its civic, inclusive outlook is inferred to reject language as the defining basis of a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal citizen participation in common institutions points against separate religious electorates; inferred, since the sources do not address them.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Port Huron Statement criticises Cold War fear politics, so claims of foreign plots are inferred to be viewed sceptically; not discussed directly.

free-public-college.rationale: The Port Huron Statement treats education and universities as sites of democratic formation, and the educative view of participation favours open access; tuition itself is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Participatory democrats prefer public decision-making on the environment and are not tied to any one tool; the sources do not say whether taxes or regulation is preferred.

future-generations.rationale: Citizens deciding collectively on community concerns, with the Port Huron call for responsibility, implies duties to those who come after; inferred, not stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Feminist participatory theorists such as Pateman argue that excluded voices change politics, but the sources do not state this; adherents may also reject essentialism.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Port Huron Statement attacks the arms race and calls for disarmament initiatives; this is applied here to the participatory-democracy tradition as a whole.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Participation requires informed citizens and public decision-making, which implies openness on treaties; inferred from the Port Huron critique of unaccountable elites.

capital-controls.rationale: Democratic control of economic resources is a theme, but the sources do not address cross-border capital and adherents differ on economic tools.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: participatory democrats want a legitimate, accountable state, not armed groups outside democratic control.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the New Left opposed war, but adherents are split on individual refusal versus democratic decision on war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Workplace democracy is central to the tradition, and collective bargaining gives workers a voice at work.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; adherents focus on participation, not the form of income support.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: fixed legal limits take budget choices away from citizens, who participatory budgeting says should decide.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron Statement's concern with global inequality and democratic control over the economy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the tradition seeks to democratise existing institutions rather than destroy and replace them.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: communities deciding their own arrangements fits local self-government, though no blueprint is documented.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents can accept or reject pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: a sacralised nation sits poorly with an emphasis on active, equal citizens.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron Statement's call for wider access to education; no stand on debt is documented.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is silent on regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron Statement's view of people as capable of self-development and worth.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: an informed citizenry needs independent media, though the tradition rarely discusses it.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; participatory democracy is a procedural view that takes no position on religious truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents differ on farm support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; the Port Huron Statement criticised the arms race and the sources otherwise do not discuss unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Port Huron Statement criticised both established parties, but adherents focus on citizen participation more than class parties, so views are split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: equal citizenship and participation imply protecting women's bodily integrity, though the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: equal participation in public life implies equal legal rights for women, though inheritance is not discussed in the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the tradition favours public participation in setting rules, including regulation, over leaving the matter to private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the tradition grounds lawmaking in broad citizen participation rather than a reserved role for traditional leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred as split: adherents back community decision-making on environmental questions but also prize individual participation and freedom.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: the Port Huron Statement criticised punitive institutions and the tradition values deliberation over fixed rules, but sentencing is not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between inclusion by requirement and by encouragement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not discussed in the sources; workplace democracy is favoured but compulsory dues are a separate issue.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the aim of widening participation; the sources do not discuss voter identification rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the principle that all citizens should take part on equal terms; not discussed in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Participatory theory treats elections alone as thin democracy and asks for citizens' direct, continuing part in decisions, as the Port Huron Statement and the Stanford entry describe.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's openness to personal freedom; premarital sex is not discussed in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the demand for open information and citizen voice; shutdowns are not discussed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not discussed in the sources; adherents could back a cash income or keep programs.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal participation of all adult citizens is the core of the idea, so excluding women from voting or office would contradict it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The sources do not address religion and women; adherents are likely split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's anti-racism in the Port Huron Statement; the scientific status of race is not discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The sources do not address gender equality agencies; adherents may prefer bottom-up bodies, but this is not stated.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: participatory democrats favour democratic community control of resources, as in the Port Huron call for public participation in economic decisions, over first-claim private ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from a general commitment to accountable power and democratic norms; the sources do not address international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is secular and procedural and rests on citizens' own reasoning; the sources do not discuss scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the principle that everyone affected should have an equal voice in decisions; the sources do not discuss Indigenous self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: participatory democrats want economic decisions opened to citizens, so a bureaucracy-run planned state is not a model, though they would oppose foreign attack; not discussed in the sources.

indirect-election.rationale: The tradition holds that citizens should take direct and continuing part in decisions rather than only choosing representatives, so layered delegate selection runs against its core.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal standing of all citizens in decisions; the sources do not address church status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on decision-making close to those affected and on decentralised participation; not discussed in the sources.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: letting affected inhabitants decide directly by vote is the tradition's central principle applied to territory, though the sources do not discuss territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the tradition has no stated position on colonial borders and its principles of local self-determination point both ways.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss lifestyle; the Port Huron Statement criticises consumerism but participation does not require simplicity.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: local control favours restrictions chosen by residents but equal participation cuts against exclusion; the sources do not address it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: adherents support gender equality but the tradition has no position on conscription, and the New Left opposed the draft.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Not a participatory-democracy question; adherents hold varied views on land and nation.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron emphasis on human dignity and citizens' control over power; no source addresses it directly.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron call for democratic control of economic resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Adherents combine individual autonomy with collective decision-making; no source settles it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not addressed by the tradition.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between universal and targeted programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Participation is meant to run through assemblies, workplaces and organised groups, so a leader bypassing them is contrary to it; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron critique of concentrated corporate power over decisions.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The tradition does not address religious organisation of politics.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to equality and equal participation; divorce law is not discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the Port Huron call for democratic public control of resources, which does not specifically address foreign ownership.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Pateman's link between social equality and equal participation, which treats large inequalities as undermining democracy.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The Port Huron Statement treats racial inequality as a central ongoing wrong, so adherents would not say racism has ceased to be a main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: New Left participants practised civil disobedience, but no source states a legal-philosophical position.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The Port Huron text values work as educative and does not take a stance on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed beyond a general Cold War critique.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed beyond general democratic ideals.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasise both economic democracy and equal recognition.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: one-party leadership contradicts direct citizen participation, though markets themselves are not the tradition's target.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should help decide how a public budget is spent, through open meetings or votes.
missingStatements.rationale: Participatory budgeting, begun in Porto Alegre in 1989, is presented as a signature participatory mechanism.

missingStatements.text: Citizens chosen by lot should be convened to deliberate and advise on major public questions.
missingStatements.rationale: Citizens' assemblies such as Ireland's 2011 assembly and France's 2019 climate convention are cited as participatory instruments.

missingStatements.text: Taking part in public decisions develops citizens' abilities and sense of responsibility.
missingStatements.rationale: Pateman holds that the major function of participation is educative, building political efficacy and skills.

notes: Strands differ: Pateman and the New Left emphasise workplace and community self-management, Fishkin and Landemore emphasise deliberation, and some adherents favour referendums while others doubt them. Port Huron's policy positions on race, war and corporations belong to the 1960s New Left rather than to participatory theory as such.
